findings.description: Your signal handler modifies a volatile bool variable (handler_invoked = true;). While volatile helps with compiler optimizations, it does not guarantee atomicity or safety in signal handlers. Only async-signal-safe functions and operations are allowed in signal handlers. On some platforms, even writing to a bool (which may be a byte or word) is not guaranteed to be atomic.
In the child process, you close pipefd[0] (the read end) and then immediately try to read(pipefd[0], ...). This is a logic error and could cause undefined behavior or a file descriptor leak.
The write() and read() calls are not checked for errors. This can lead to silent failures.
If fork() fails, both ends of the pipe remain open.
